focus: fail-closed projectId scoping on the SUBSCRIBE target DB-lookup, IDOR, cross-tenant leak
summary: The SUBSCRIBE target lookup is correctly fail-closed by projectId. resolveSubscribeTarget loads via findById (not DB-project-scoped) then applies an explicit .filter(projectId.equals(f.getProjectId())) before returning — the same anti-IDOR guard as requireFunnel. Missing id, malformed ObjectId, and foreign-project id all collapse to a single funnel_subscribe_target_not_found code (no existence oracle, no cross-tenant leak). Malformed ObjectId is caught and mapped to 422, never 500. No user input is logged. Same fail-closed resolve is reused on the activation path. No vulnerabilities found.

findings.title: Project-scope guard verified present on every target resolution
findings.detail: Both save (validateSubscribeTarget) and activation (requireSubscribeTargetsActive) route through resolveSubscribeTarget, which enforces projectId.equals(target.getProjectId()) post-load. Callers (update/activate/testRun) all run requireFunnel/requireOwned FIRST, so projectId is already proven owned by the caller before it is used as the scope. No cross-tenant target binding is reachable.
findings.reason: Correct as implemented; recorded for traceability.
